cards.explanation: The answer is the synagogues, friends. Verse 20 says Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus there. He went where the community gathered and said it out loud. Most of us need three practice runs just to order at a drive-through.

The answer is “He is the Son of God.” Those are Saul's words, and they're big ones. Saul wasn't just saying nice things about Jesus. He was saying who Jesus is. I'd say that's pretty bold, wouldn't you?

The answer is astounded, friends. That's the word in verse 21. Hearing Saul preach Jesus knocked the people sideways, and they even start asking questions about it. I'd be asking questions too, and I'd be holding my hat.

The answer is False. Saul doesn't go quiet. Acts 9:22 says he was empowered all the more. He confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. When I get stared at, I forget my own name, so that's impressive.

The answer is by proving that Jesus is the Christ. Verse 22 says that's how Saul confounded the Jews living in Damascus. The text gives his proving as the way he did it, and they were confounded. I know that feeling, mostly from group chats.
The answer is True. Verse 24 says Saul learned of their plot. He knew people were out to kill him. That's a heavy thing to know, and I think it must have weighed on him.

The answer is in a basket through a window. His disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall, and they did it one night. With the gates watched day and night, a window was the way out. I've been stuck in some tight spots myself, but nobody ever lowered me out of one in a basket.

The answer is that they are all afraid of him. Verse 26 says they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple. I think that was a hard door to knock on, friends. Saul tried to join them, and fear is what he met.

The answer is the apostles, friends. Verse 27 says Barnabas, a Levite from Cyprus (Acts 4:36), brought Saul to them. Then Barnabas told them how Saul had seen the Lord. I think that was a kind thing to do.

The answer is how he spoke boldly in Damascus. Verse 27 says Barnabas described how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus. So the apostles heard about the road and about Damascus. Barnabas gave them what he knew, and I think that's what changed the room.

The answer is True. Verse 29 says Saul talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him. That's a heavy turn after verse 28, where he's moving about freely. I think this part hurts.
The answer is Tarsus, friends. Verse 30 says the brothers took Saul down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus. His friends looked out for him. I think they cared about keeping him safe.

The answer is a time of peace. Verse 31 says the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers. It lived in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit. And that's the end of this passage. But this story isn't over, friends.
